exact_statement: For any sign Boolean f(z,x) with s>=1 physical uniform core coordinates and d>=1 data coordinates, supply each nonconstant slice with a normalized nonempty reference q_z covering its nonempty Fourier support. Let qbar be the uniform mixture over the k nonconstant slices (uniform data reference if k=0), fixed before the target. Define Q(empty,B)=1/[2(2^s-1)] for nonempty core B and Q(A,B)=qbar(A)/2^(s+1) for nonempty data A and every core B. This normalized reference covers the actual spectrum. With M=E_z Var(f_z), N=sum_{B nonempty} fhat(empty,B)^2, Gamma=E_z sum_{A nonempty} f_z_hat(A)^2 log2(q_z(A)/qbar(A)), its EXACT complete nonempty cost is E_z C_z+Gamma+(s+1)M+[1+log2(2^s-1)]N, and Gamma<=M log2(k)<=sM when k>0, Gamma=0 otherwise. If K>=0 and C_z<=K I(f_z), then C_Q<=K I_x+(2s+1)M+(s+1)N<=(K+2s+1)I, full wrapped cost<=(K+2s+3)I. In particular all actual conjunctions of clauses OR(Z_Tj,X_j), T_j arbitrary subsets of TWO shared bits and X_j disjoint private blocks of arbitrary positive widths, have an explicit strictly positive Q with complete nonempty cost<=13I and full cost<=15I, using once-paid half-activation clause masks. For the SAME uniform-core reference on odd majority cores s=2m+1 with a dummy data bit, nonempty cost/I>=sqrt(m+1), so this growing-core reference is not universally influence-paid. No free reset, unsigned alias pushforward, or unlimited-depth closure is asserted. Moreover the SAME code on the actual positive-private-clause family with odd s=2m+1>=3 core, every size-m+1 anchor T repeated s times as OR(z_T,x_T,l) with fresh single-bit private blocks, satisfies C_Q/I>=(5/16)sqrt(m+1). Its core-only mass N>=5/8 and actual physical influence I<=2I(Maj_s). Thus uniform-core payment fails even inside this clause class with nonempty private blocks, not merely on a dummy-data control.

exact_statement: For EVERY nonconstant Boolean core g on s>=1 bits and every integer L>=1, introduce L fresh positive private variables for each false core point v and take F_L=2 product_{v:g(v)=-1,l}(a_v(z) OR x_vl)-1, where a_v is the signed core clause false exactly at v. All private bits are relevant, the displayed CNF is irredundant and each displayed clause is a prime implicate (not necessarily the complete prime table). With q=Pr[g=-1] and epsilon=2^-L, every nonempty core-only coefficient is (1-epsilon)ghat(S), the empty coefficient is (1-epsilon)ghat(empty)+epsilon, and I(F_L)=(1-epsilon)^2 I(g)+2qepsilon[s(1-epsilon)+L]. Every nonempty private Fourier set lies in one private group, with coefficient magnitude 2^(1-s)epsilon for every core set; all cross-group private coefficients vanish. Thus private spectral mass is 4qepsilon(1-epsilon), its entropy is that mass times(2s+2L-2), H(F_L)->H(g), and H(F_L)/I(F_L)->H(g)/I(g). The supremum H/I on this actual signed-core positive-private clause family equals that over ALL Boolean functions, so same-constant FEI on this family is equivalent to full FEI. For ANY fixed normalized or subprobability nonempty reference R covering F_L, with core-sector mass Z_c>0 and r_c=R_core/Z_c, the EXACT extraction identity is C_g(r_c)=C_core(F_L;R)/(1-epsilon)^2+Var(g)log2 Z_c. The NEGATIVE normalization is retained. For the finite L=4s+4, C(F_L;R)<=K I(F_L) implies C_g(r_c)<=2K I(g). No influence-paid R for arbitrary cores is constructed, and no equivalence for all-positive core anchors or FEI resolution is claimed.
